justification: Assessment reported INVALID and targets the same defect as ground truth: the proof's conclusion that greedy 'dispatch the nearest available ambulance' is globally optimal, reached by collapsing incident positions into L/R buckets with fixed average trip lengths. Its witness is a different-but-valid instance of the same claim (it stays in the post's own A,B at 0 / C at 1 configuration and varies the first-incident position rather than moving an ambulance to 1/2). I verified the arithmetic independently: at t1=0.6, sending C costs 0.4 + E[t2]=0.5 = 0.90 while sending A costs 0.6 + E[min(t2,1-t2)]=0.25 = 0.85; the crossover is 2*t1-1 = 0.25 at t1=0.625. Policy expectations: greedy (threshold 0.5) = 0.125+0.125+0.125+0.25 = 0.625; threshold-0.625 policy = 0.1953125+0.15625+0.0703125+0.1875 = 0.609375. These are exactly the ground truth's E[greedy]=5/8 and E[optimal]=39/64 with the same 1/64 gap, so the assessment refutes the same optimality claim with a correct witness.
